scope: 16 exact PHYS cards only; prerequisite references are conditions, not recursively inventoried obligations.

PHYS-211.name: University Physics I
PHYS-211.description: Calculus-based mechanics, gravitation, conservation laws, rotation, equilibrium, oscillations and waves with integrated experimental/data work.
PHYS-211.prerequisites: Prerequisites: C- or better in MATH-171 or MATH-181 or equivalent course. Co-requisites: MATH-172 or MATH-182 or equivalent course.

category_review.locator: PHYS-211 complete current public course card
category_review.rationale: Physical laws and experimental mechanics are the primary subject despite calculus support.

PHYS-212.name: University Physics II
PHYS-212.description: Electrostatics, circuits, magnetic fields, induction and optics in an integrated lecture/laboratory format.
PHYS-212.prerequisites: Prerequisites: (PHYS-211 or PHYS-211A or PHYS-206 or PHYS-216) or (MECE-102, MECE-103 and MECE-205) and (MATH-182 or MATH-172 or MATH-182A) or equivalent courses. Grades of C- or better are required in all prerequisite courses.

category_review.locator: PHYS-212 complete current public course card
category_review.rationale: The description teaches electricity, magnetism and optics as physical domain knowledge.

PHYS-213.name: Modern Physics I
PHYS-213.description: Introductory quantum physics and relativistic dynamics, including photons, wave-particle duality, wave mechanics, atomic models and spin.
PHYS-213.prerequisites: Prerequisites: PHYS-209 or PHYS-212 or PHYS-217or equivalent course.

category_review.locator: PHYS-213 complete current public course card
category_review.rationale: Modern physical concepts and atomic phenomena form the course focus.

PHYS-283.name: Vibrations and Waves
PHYS-283.description: Harmonic, damped and driven oscillators, coupled oscillators and continuous vibrating systems across physical settings.
PHYS-283.prerequisites: Prerequisites: PHYS-212 or PHYS-217 or PHYS-209 and (MATH-182 or MATH-182A or MATH-173) or equivalent courses. Co-requisites: MATH-231 or equivalent course.

category_review.locator: PHYS-283 complete current public course card
category_review.rationale: Oscillatory physical systems are the substantive topic; mathematical models support that domain.

PHYS-315.name: Experiments in Modern Physics
PHYS-315.description: Experiments on early quantum phenomena and physical constants, using instrumentation, data reduction, laboratory notebooks and journal-style reporting.
PHYS-315.prerequisites: Prerequisites: PHYS-213 or equivalent course and (PHYS-BS or PHYS-MN or PHYS-IM) program students.

category_review.locator: PHYS-315 complete current public course card
category_review.rationale: Experimental physics and measurement practice dominate; writing communicates the scientific work.

PHYS-320.name: Mathematical Methods in Physics
PHYS-320.description: Matrix algebra, vector calculus, Fourier analysis, partial differential equations and series solutions of ordinary differential equations.
PHYS-320.prerequisites: Prerequisites: (MATH-219 or MATH-221) and MATH-231 and (PHYS-209 or PHYS-212 or PHYS-217) or equivalent courses.

category_review.locator: PHYS-320 complete current public course card
category_review.rationale: The actual course teaches mathematical tools and solution methods, with physics as the motivating application.

PHYS-330.name: Classical Mechanics
PHYS-330.description: Newtonian motion, conservation, non-inertial frames, central forces, Lagrangian mechanics and rigid-body motion using advanced mathematical techniques.
PHYS-330.prerequisites: Prerequisites: (MATH-219 or MATH-221) and MATH-231 and (PHYS-209 or PHYS-212 or PHYS-217). Students in the PHYS-BS program are also required to complete PHYS-275 prior to taking this course. Co-requisites: PHYS-320 or equivalent course.

category_review.locator: PHYS-330 complete current public course card
category_review.rationale: The central subject is physical mechanics; mathematics supplies its formal representation.

PHYS-411.name: Electricity and Magnetism
PHYS-411.description: Charges, currents, fields, materials, Maxwell equations and waves, including vector-calculus formalisms and boundary-value methods.
PHYS-411.prerequisites: Prerequisites: (PHYS-209 or PHYS-212 or PHYS-217) and PHYS-320 or equivalent courses. Students in PHYS-BS or PHYS-2M are also required to complete PHYS-275 prior to taking this course.

category_review.locator: PHYS-411 complete current public course card
category_review.rationale: Electromagnetic phenomena and field theory are the primary domain, rather than a general mathematical-methods survey.

PHYS-414.name: Quantum Mechanics
PHYS-414.description: Nonrelativistic quantum mechanics: wave functions, Schrödinger equations, states, operators, commutators, uncertainty and angular momentum.
PHYS-414.prerequisites: Prerequisites: PHYS-213 and (PHYS-320 or (MATH-231 and (MATH-241 or MATH-241H))) or equivalent courses.

category_review.locator: PHYS-414 complete current public course card
category_review.rationale: The formal structure is used to study quantum physical systems; no AI-methods content is stated.

PHYS-440.name: Thermal and Statistical Physics
PHYS-440.description: Thermodynamics and its statistical basis, entropy, equilibrium, potentials, gas kinetics and classical/quantum statistics.
PHYS-440.prerequisites: Prerequisites: PHYS-213 and MATH-231 or equivalent courses. Students in the PHYS-BS program are also required to complete PHYS-275 prior to taking this course.

category_review.locator: PHYS-440 complete current public course card
category_review.rationale: Statistical reasoning supports thermodynamics and physical equilibrium, the central subject.

PHYS-220.name: University Astronomy
PHYS-220.description: Astronomical and astrophysical concepts, celestial mechanics, observational methods, planetary and stellar systems, cosmology and life.
PHYS-220.prerequisites: Prerequisites: PHYS-211 or PHYS-211A or PHYS-207 or PHYS-216 or (MECE-102 and MECE-103 and MECE-205) or equivalent courses.

category_review.locator: PHYS-220 complete current public course card
category_review.rationale: The description surveys astronomy and astrophysics as domain science.

PHYS-370.name: Stellar Astrophysics
PHYS-370.description: Stellar observations, atmospheres, structure/evolution, interactions with interstellar matter and Milky Way populations.
PHYS-370.prerequisites: Prerequisites: PHYS-213 and PHYS-220 or equivalent courses. Students in the PHYS-BS program are also required to complete PHYS-275 prior to taking this course.

category_review.locator: PHYS-370 complete current public course card
category_review.rationale: Stars and their astrophysical processes are the primary content.

PHYS-371.name: Galactic Astrophysics
PHYS-371.description: Milky Way structure and dynamics, major components, interactions and observational methods.
PHYS-371.prerequisites: Prerequisites: PHYS-213 and PHYS-220 or equivalent courses. Students in the PHYS-BS program are also required to complete PHYS-275 prior to taking this course.

category_review.locator: PHYS-371 complete current public course card
category_review.rationale: The course studies our galaxy and methods of astronomical investigation.

PHYS-372.name: Extragalactic Astrophysics and Cosmology
PHYS-372.description: Large-scale cosmic structure, galaxies/clusters, cosmic history and evidence for cosmological parameters.
PHYS-372.prerequisites: Prerequisites: PHYS-213 and PHYS-220 or equivalent courses. Students in the PHYS-BS program are also required to complete PHYS-275 prior to taking this course.

category_review.locator: PHYS-372 complete current public course card
category_review.rationale: The full description centers on cosmological physical phenomena and evidence.

PHYS-373.name: Observational Astronomy
PHYS-373.description: Practical optical astronomy with telescopes/CCD cameras, image reduction, removal of instrumental effects and analysis.
PHYS-373.prerequisites: Prerequisites: PHYS-220 or equivalent course. Students in the PHYS-BS program are also required to complete PHYS-275 prior to taking this course.

category_review.locator: PHYS-373 complete current public course card
category_review.rationale: Astronomical instrumentation and image-analysis practice are domain applications, not general software foundations.

PHYS-251.name: Introduction to Quantum Technology
PHYS-251.description: Quantum concepts and mathematics applied to sensing, computation and material simulation, with device challenges, visualization tools and societal context.
PHYS-251.prerequisites: Prerequisites: (PHYS-111 or PHYS-207 or PHYS-211 or PHYS-211A or PHYS-216) and (MATH-172 or MATH-182 or MATH-182A) or equivalent courses.

category_review.locator: PHYS-251 complete current public course card
category_review.rationale: The course introduces quantum physical concepts and their technological applications; it does not specify an AI-methods or classical computing-systems sequence.
